We want to understand what you meant by "the "Continue Shopping" part feels very prominent, almost maybe too much?", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The "Continue Shopping" button is placed above the "Place Order" button, making it appear higher in the hierarchy than the checkout action.
B) The "Continue Shopping" button takes up a large full-width area near the bottom, so it visually dominates the button section.
C) The "Place Order" button appears visually muted compared with "Continue Shopping," making the order completion option feel buried or secondary in the layout.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: C, I think. I mean, B is also true visually, and A probably contributes, but the thing that really made me pause was that “Place Order” looks disabled or almost unavailable while “Continue Shopping” is the strongest thing on the page. So the action that should complete the checkout feels kind of buried under the action that takes you away from checkout, if that’s fair. But maybe that’s only because the fields are empty, so I might be reading the state too strongly.

turns.q: When you noticed the full-width “Continue Shopping” button dominating that lower section, what information or option were you expecting to stand out there instead?
turns.a: I think I expected the thing that advances the purchase to be the dominant element there, so probably “Place Order,” or at least some clear message saying why it isn’t available yet. The lower section feels like the decision point after Payment Details, and the strongest option is basically an exit route, which is a bit… I don’t know, backwards maybe. If “Place Order” has to stay disabled until the card fields are filled, I’d expect the disabled state to be visually connected to the missing payment inputs, not separated by this big black “Continue Shopping” button. But I might be assuming too much from a static wireframe, sorry.

turns.q: You mentioned wanting “Place Order” or an explanation to stand out there—what about the current full-width “Continue Shopping” layout makes that hard to achieve?
turns.a: The “Continue Shopping” button is using the same big full-width button shape I’d normally associate with the final checkout action, but it gets the darker, active treatment, so it sort of consumes the whole action area before “Place Order” even has a chance to explain itself. The grey “Place Order” underneath then reads like an afterthought, or like a disabled secondary control, not the main outcome of filling in Payment Details. Also, the small terms text is below it, which usually belongs to the purchase commitment, but visually it’s attached to this muted button rather than helping clarify the state. I could be wrong, but I think the layout is asking one button to be the primary visual anchor and another button to be the primary task, and those are split.

turns.q: Which part of the lower layout were you checking when the full-width “Continue Shopping” button first pulled your attention?
turns.a: I think my eye was coming out of the Payment Details card, especially that faint “We accept Visa…” line, and then the next strong thing underneath is the black full-width “Continue Shopping” button. So I wasn’t initially comparing both buttons equally; I was following the vertical path from the fields down to what looked like the next action. The grey “Place Order” only registered after that, almost like a disabled follow-up below the real button, which is maybe the problem. Sorry, that sounds very specific for a first glance, but that’s where my attention went.

turns.q: What should the lower action area communicate as the primary purpose of the checkout screen, given that “Continue Shopping” currently dominates that space?
turns.a: It should probably communicate, very plainly, that the purpose of this screen is to finish the order after entering payment details, not to go back into shopping. Like, the bottom area should make “complete checkout” feel like the destination, even if “Place Order” is temporarily disabled until the empty card fields are filled. Right now the strongest visual message is “leave this flow,” and the purchase action is sort of waiting underneath it without much explanation. I’d expect maybe the disabled “Place Order” to be first or visually tied to a note like “Enter payment details to place order,” with “Continue Shopping” treated more like a secondary link, but maybe that’s too prescriptive.
